policy: Every shipped image has an id, role, screen, path, dimensions, source, rights, approval and validation here.
No author name or byline anywhere; covers are cropped above the author line.

No image-generation capability was available in this production session: nothing here is AI-generated for r7. The 260-asset backlog from the brief is scoped in docs/ART_BACKLOG.md with prompts and acceptance criteria for a future, reviewed batch.
The concept collage and the rejected simplistic art pack are not used.

r7.1: the Illustrated Revision drives the whole UI. Its paintings are cut to each slot’s exact aspect and retouched (soft-focus grade, grain) for the landing/welcome screens, the Hub and every room’s back wall; its navigation discs and winged badges are cut out as individual transparent assets and used as the app’s icons and badges; its button and title language is rebuilt in CSS/canvas. Not used: aircraft and instrument sheets (supplier-flagged unverified), character portraits (author’s decision).

r7.2: the illustrator's delivery against docs/ART_GENERATION_BRIEF.pdf replaces the concept upscales file-for-file (44 of 46 delivered; 2 rejected, 2 missing badges derived in-house, 10 files mechanically repaired). docs/ART_ACCEPTANCE.md records every decision; docs/ART_INTEGRATION_LOG.json is the machine record. 22 of the delivered files were exported from 512-px previews by the illustrator and remain soft; round 2 (docs/ART_ROUND2_CORRECTIONS.pdf) asks for the originals.

r7.3: the illustrator's three raw-download ZIPs (33 files: the 22 full-size originals of delivered files and 11 extra generations; none of the 22 preview-based files) were triaged file by file in docs/ART_ACCEPTANCE.md. Used: five extra badge arts, the dusk apron panorama (the runway horizon, stitched so its aircraft is left out) and the full-size FBO original (repaired). Every room was then checked whole against the app's own stations, and painted objects that duplicated them were painted out (lounge, classroom, game room); the wash-pad and game-room floors were calmed; a military roundel and an extra tail wheel came off the FBO trainer; a fighter came out of the classroom tile's window.

drawnInCode.icons: Every UI icon (hfq_ui.js IC) and every canvas icon (icons.js) is drawn in code: one stroke family on a 24-unit grid. No raster icon files ship.
drawnInCode.figures: Instructional figures (G.FIG in hfq_figs.js: the four forces, the six-pack, airport signs, lights, markings) are drawn in code from FAA references and are the only images used in assessments. Generative mockups are not used for exam items.
drawnInCode.world: The airfield rooms' stations, crew, props and aircraft are the r6.6 canvas art, repainted in the navy/brass palette (theme.js), set against the commissioned back walls, skies and floors. FAA signs, markings and lights keep their standard colors by design and are always drawn by code (the ramp and runway floors therefore stay code-drawn).
